description: List the organization's monitor and heartbeat incidents, newest first (or by attention with sort), to see what is or was down and which alerts went out. Each item has id, monitor_id or heartbeat_id (exactly one is set), monitor (id, name and type) and heartbeat (id and name), of which one is null, started_at, created_at, resolved_at (null while open), cause, cause_detail (the raw check error), acknowledged_at, acknowledged_by_user (id and name; may be null on an acknowledged incident: a Telegram acknowledgement, an older one, or a deleted user) and notification_logs: the alerts sent, oldest first, each with id, channel_type (EMAIL, TELEGRAM, WEBHOOK, SLACK or DISCORD), destination (may be masked), channel_label (the channel's label when the alert was sent; can be null), event (TRIGGERED for the first alert only, RESOLVED for the recovery; reminders are not logged per incident), sent_at, status (PENDING while a webhook, Slack or Discord delivery is still being tried, then SENT or FAILED) and error (the last delivery error). started_at is the outage start: the first failing check of the streak (for a heartbeat, the missed deadline, or when the /fail ping arrived). created_at is when the incident was confirmed and its first alert went out, often minutes after started_at. resolved_at is when it ended: the check that confirmed recovery, or the pause, deletion or plan downgrade that closed it (null while open). acknowledged_at is when someone acknowledged it (null if nobody has). An incident's duration is resolved_at minus started_at. For one incident's full record use get_incident; for the checks behind it use list_check_results; incidents posted on a status page are list_status_page_incidents. An incident resolves by itself when its monitor or heartbeat recovers. Returns a page: items plus total, page, size and pages. An invalid value is a 422 naming the argument. Example: {"status": "open", "size": 50}

all_time.description: true lists incidents of all time, one page at a time. Not together with period_days, from or to.

cause.description: Keep one failure cause, such as TIMEOUT, HTTP_5XX or HEARTBEAT_MISSED.

from.description: First UTC date of a calendar range, YYYY-MM-DD, inclusive. An incident is listed if it was active on any day of the range. Not together with period_days.

heartbeat_id.description: Keep one heartbeat's incidents: its uuid from list_heartbeats. Not together with monitor_id (a 422).

monitor_id.description: Keep one monitor's incidents: its uuid from list_monitors. Not together with heartbeat_id (a 422).

period_days.description: Keep incidents active within the last N days, 1 to 365. Without period_days, from, to or all_time the tool lists the last 30 days.

q.description: Case-insensitive substring of the monitor's or heartbeat's current name, up to 255 characters.

size.description: Rows per page, 1 to 100; default 25. Keep paging until you have seen total rows.

sort.description: attention: open unacknowledged first, then open acknowledged, then resolved; newest first within each. Omit it for newest first.

status.description: open or resolved (lowercase); omit it for both.

to.description: Last UTC date of a calendar range, YYYY-MM-DD, inclusive; without it the range runs to now. Not together with period_days.

name: list_incidents

acknowledged_at.description: When someone acknowledged the incident; null if nobody has.

name.description: The user's current first and last name.

acknowledged_by_user.description: The Fettle user behind acknowledged_by; null while unacknowledged, for a Telegram tap, for an acknowledgement recorded before the source was stored and for a user deleted since.

anyOf.description: Known values: DASHBOARD, API_KEY, MCP, TELEGRAM.

cause.description: Known values: TIMEOUT, DNS_FAILURE, CONNECTION_REFUSED, TLS_INVALID, HTTP_4XX, HTTP_5XX, HTTP_UNEXPECTED_STATUS, KEYWORD_MISSING, TOO_MANY_REDIRECTS, TARGET_BLOCKED, PORT_STATE_MISMATCH, INVALID_TARGET, HEARTBEAT_MISSED, HEARTBEAT_FAILED, UNKNOWN.

created_at.description: When the incident was confirmed (after the monitor's confirmation rounds) and its first alert went out; at or after started_at, usually by seconds to minutes.

heartbeat.description: The heartbeat that failed; null for a monitor.

last_notified_at.description: When the Down alert went out; null until it has been sent. On incidents opened before reminder digests it can be the last repeat alert instead.

type.description: Known values: HTTP, PING, SSL, TCP, DNS.

monitor.description: The monitor that failed; null for a heartbeat.

channel_label.description: The channel's label when the alert was sent. A later rename or delete of the channel does not change it. Null for a channel without a label, for a member's own email channel, for a fallback email, and on rows sent before labels were recorded.

channel_type.description: Known values: EMAIL, TELEGRAM, WEBHOOK, SLACK, DISCORD.

event.description: Known values: TRIGGERED, RESOLVED, SSL_EXPIRY, SSL_RENEWAL_OVERDUE, SSL_COVERAGE_LOST, CHANGE_DETECTED, DOMAIN_EXPIRY, DOMAIN_ON_HOLD, DOMAIN_NOT_IN_REGISTRY, REMINDER.

renotify_count.description: How many reminders listed this incident.

resolved_at.description: When the incident ended: the check that confirmed recovery (for a heartbeat, the ping that brought it back), or the pause, deletion or plan downgrade that closed it; null while the incident is open.

started_at.description: When the outage started: the first failing check of the streak, at or before created_at. For a heartbeat, the missed deadline (last ping plus period and grace), or when the /fail ping arrived. Duration and downtime count from here.

title: List incidents
